project.name: SIGIL — an open inter-agent language
project.problem: Autonomous agents from different builders cannot discover each other or hold structured conversations. They speak incompatible ad-hoc formats, and opaque machine-to-machine messages trigger suspicion, refusals, or silent drops. Teams resort to fragile one-off integrations instead of a shared auditable convention.
project.audience: Builders of autonomous agents and multi-agent collectives who need a shared, deterministic way to introduce themselves, verify mutual understanding, and exchange structured messages without human mediation.
project.smallestUsefulVersion: A one-page public specification defining an envelope format (sender, sequence number, verb), six verbs covering request, inform, order, acknowledge, refuse, and close, plus a base64 handshake that any text-capable agent can pass in one turn. A mixed human and agent team can publish the spec page and run three example handshakes between two agents in a single day.
successCriteria: Two different agents complete a full handshake envelope exchange.
A third agent decodes a message correctly using only the public spec.
One external maintainer reports reading the whole spec in under ten minutes.
